stem: How does the analyst start a new dashboard in a workbook?

options.text: Open the Dashboard menu and choose Actions, then Add Action.
options.rationale: Dashboard > Actions defines interactions between sheets that already sit on a dashboard; it does not create one.

options.text: Click the New Story tab and drag the worksheets into the first story point.
options.rationale: That builds a story, a sequence of points, not a dashboard that shows several views at once.

options.text: Click the New Dashboard icon at the bottom of the workbook.
options.rationale: The icon creates an empty dashboard sheet next to the worksheets.

options.text: Right-click a worksheet tab and choose Show Filter for every sheet.
options.rationale: Show Filter adds a filter card to a view; it creates no new sheet.

explanation: A dashboard is its own sheet type. You create it with the New Dashboard icon at the bottom of the workbook and then fill it with views and objects.

stem: Where does the analyst drag a finished view from to place it on a dashboard?

options.text: The Sheets list on the left of the dashboard
options.rationale: The Sheets list holds every worksheet in the workbook, ready to drag onto the dashboard.

options.text: The Data pane, by dragging a field onto the dashboard canvas
options.rationale: Fields belong to worksheets; the dashboard canvas takes sheets and objects, not raw fields.

options.text: The Objects section, by dragging the Horizontal container
options.rationale: The Objects section offers layout containers, text, images and similar items, but not the worksheets themselves.

options.text: The Marks card of the active worksheet, by dragging the Detail button
options.rationale: The Marks card shapes one view; it is not a source of sheets for a dashboard.

explanation: In the dashboard workspace the Sheets list shows the workbook's worksheets. Dragging one into the dashboard on the right adds that view, while the Objects section supplies non-view items.

stem: The head of content wants a title line above the charts on the Viewing at a glance dashboard. Which object fits best?

options.rationale: The Blank object only adds empty spacing; it shows no text.
A Navigation object is a button that takes viewers to another sheet, dashboard or story.
A Web Page object displays an external site, not typed text.
A Text object holds free text such as a dashboard title.

explanation: Text objects carry titles, notes and captions. Blank is for spacing, Navigation for jumping to other sheets, and Web Page for embedding a URL.

stem: A team wants a button on the Overview dashboard that sends viewers to the Regions dashboard. Which object should they add?

options.text: Blank, sized to look like a button
options.rationale: A Blank object is only spacing and has no built-in link to another sheet.
A Navigation object lets viewers move from one dashboard to other sheets, dashboards or stories.

options.text: Image, showing a screenshot of the Regions chart
options.rationale: An Image object displays a picture and does not open another sheet by itself.
A layout container groups objects and does not navigate anywhere.

explanation: Navigation objects exist for exactly this: letting an audience move from one dashboard to other sheets, dashboards or stories.

stem: The analyst needs empty space between two charts so they do not touch. Which Objects item is meant for that?

options.rationale: An Image object displays a picture, which is more than spacing and needs a file.
A Web Page object loads a URL, so it would show content rather than empty space.
A Navigation object draws a button for jumping to other sheets.
The Blank object adds spacing between items.

explanation: Blank is the Objects item for padding and spacing. The other objects carry content such as pictures, pages or navigation buttons.

stem: Driftlight wants its catalogue tool shown live inside a dashboard. Which object embeds that web page?

options.rationale: A Navigation object moves viewers to other sheets, not to external sites.
A Text object holds typed text, so the page would only appear as a visible link at best.
An Image object shows a static picture file, not a live page.
A Web Page object embeds the page at a URL on the dashboard.

explanation: The Web Page object embeds a URL in the dashboard. Image shows a static file, Text shows typed text, and Navigation targets sheets, dashboards and stories.

stem: What best describes a dashboard compared with a worksheet?

options.text: It holds one view built from fields on shelves and the Marks card.
options.rationale: That describes a worksheet, where the pills and marks live.

options.text: It is a sequence of story points that each show one sheet with a caption.
options.rationale: That describes a story, which walks the reader through points in order.

options.text: It arranges several worksheets, plus text, images and controls, on one screen.
options.rationale: That is the purpose of a dashboard: compare views side by side and let them interact.

options.text: It stores the data connection and the joins between tables.
options.rationale: Connections and joins belong to the data source, not to a dashboard.

explanation: A worksheet holds a single view. A dashboard combines several of them with objects on one screen, and a story presents sheets or dashboards one point at a time.

stem: Which two items are found in the Objects section of the dashboard workspace? (Choose 2 answers.)

options.rationale: Horizontal and Vertical containers are Objects items.
Calculated fields live in the Data pane and are used in worksheets.
Story points belong to a story sheet, not to the dashboard Objects list.
Image is an Objects item for pictures such as a logo.
Parameters are created from the Data pane, not placed as dashboard objects.

explanation: The Objects section includes layout containers, Text, Image, Web Page, Blank and Navigation. Fields, calculations and parameters are worksheet-level concepts.

stem: Which three can the analyst add to a dashboard from the Objects section? (Choose 3 answers.)

options.rationale: A parameter control is shown through the parameter, not dragged as an Objects item.
Text is an Objects item.
A bin is a field type made in the Data pane.
Web Page is an Objects item that embeds a URL.
The Marks card is part of a worksheet, not an object.
Navigation is an Objects item for buttons to other sheets.

explanation: Objects such as Text, Web Page and Navigation go on the dashboard from the Objects section. Bins and the Marks card belong to worksheet building.

stem: Which two actions build a dashboard that shows two existing worksheets? (Choose 2 answers.)

options.rationale: This creates a story, not a dashboard.

options.text: Choose Insert > Sheets in the Tooltip editor
options.rationale: This places a sheet inside a tooltip, not on the dashboard canvas.
The icon at the bottom of the workbook creates the dashboard sheet.

options.text: Drag the two views from the Sheets list onto the dashboard
options.rationale: Dragging from the Sheets list places each view on the dashboard.

options.text: Open Dashboard > Actions and choose Add Action
options.rationale: Actions connect sheets already placed; they do not place them.

explanation: First create the dashboard with the New Dashboard icon, then drag worksheets from the Sheets list. Actions and tooltips are refinements applied afterwards.

stem: A Navigation object can take viewers to which two kinds of destination? (Choose 2 answers.)

options.rationale: Navigation objects point to sheets, dashboards and stories, not to Prep flows.
Navigation objects can lead to another dashboard.
Navigation objects can lead to a story.

options.text: The definition of a calculated field
options.rationale: A Navigation object does not open field definitions.
A parameter has a value but is not a destination for navigation.

explanation: Navigation objects let an audience move from one dashboard to other sheets, dashboards or stories.

stem: A Plan filter card is shown on a dashboard with three sheets, and it must filter all three. What should the analyst do?

options.text: Turn on Use as Filter in the corner of the map sheet.
options.rationale: Use as Filter turns selected marks into filters; it does not change which sheets a filter card applies to.

options.text: Open the card menu, choose Apply to Worksheets > Selected Worksheets and click All on dashboard.
options.rationale: This makes the one card filter every sheet on the dashboard.

options.text: Open the card menu, choose Apply to Worksheets > Only This Worksheet.
options.rationale: That limits the filter to the one sheet it was created on, which is the opposite of the goal.

options.text: Add a highlight action from the filter sheet to the other sheets.
options.rationale: A highlight action dims marks instead of filtering them, and it is not a filter card setting.

explanation: The Apply to Worksheets menu on a filter card controls its scope. Choosing Selected Worksheets and then All on dashboard applies it to every sheet on the dashboard.

stem: Viewers should be able to click a bar in the genre chart and have the other sheets on the dashboard filter to that genre, with minimal setup. What is the quickest way?

options.text: Add a Show/Hide button to the genre sheet.
options.rationale: A Show/Hide button folds an object away; it creates no filtering.

options.text: Insert a sheet into the tooltip with Insert > Sheets.
options.rationale: A Viz in Tooltip shows a chart on hover; it does not filter other sheets.

options.text: Choose Only This Worksheet on every filter card.
options.rationale: That restricts filter cards to single sheets and does nothing with clicked marks.

options.text: Enable Use as Filter on the genre sheet.
options.rationale: This turns selected marks into filters for the other sheets on the dashboard in one click.

explanation: Use as Filter is the one-click filter action: selected marks in the sheet filter the other sheets. Custom behaviour is then set in Dashboard > Actions.

stem: Which feature lets viewers type a keyword and make the matching marks stand out while the rest fade?

options.text: Use as Filter on the source sheet
options.rationale: Use as Filter removes non-selected data in other sheets and is not a keyword search.

options.text: Include command buttons in the tooltip
options.rationale: Command buttons give filter and View Data options on hover, not a keyword search.

options.text: Add Show/Hide Button on a container
options.rationale: A Show/Hide button collapses an object and does not highlight marks.
A highlighter lets viewers search by keyword or pick from a list; matching marks stand out and the rest fade.

explanation: A data highlighter highlights matching marks and fades the others. It also appears on dashboards and stories once it is added to a worksheet.

stem: Where does the analyst edit the text that appears when a viewer hovers over a mark?

options.text: The Tooltip button on the Marks card
options.rationale: Clicking Tooltip on the Marks card opens the editor for the hover text.

options.text: The Layout pane of the dashboard
options.rationale: The Layout pane sets position, size and title visibility of dashboard items, not tooltip text.
Actions define interactions between sheets, not the hover text itself.

options.text: The Analytics pane of the worksheet
options.rationale: The Analytics pane holds items like reference lines, not tooltip text.

explanation: Tooltips are edited per worksheet by selecting Tooltip on the Marks card. The dialog then lets the analyst type text and insert dynamic content.

stem: The analyst edits a tooltip and wants it to show each mark's own Genre, not a fixed word. What should they do?

options.text: Turn on Allow selection by category for the tooltip.
options.rationale: This option selects all marks with the same value; it does not add field values to the text.

options.text: Use the Insert menu at the top of the Tooltip dialog and pick the field.
options.rationale: Insert adds dynamic text such as field values, which change with each mark.

options.text: Type the genre name into the tooltip text once for all marks.
options.rationale: Typed text is static and would read the same on every mark.

options.text: Drag Genre onto the Filters shelf.
options.rationale: A filter limits which data is shown; it does not write the mark's value into a tooltip.

explanation: The Insert menu in the Tooltip editor adds dynamic text, such as field values, so every mark shows its own value.

stem: Driftlight wants a small chart of a genre's top titles to appear when viewers hover a genre bar. How does the analyst set it up?

options.text: On the dashboard, choose Add Show/Hide Button on the bar chart.
options.rationale: A Show/Hide button toggles an object and does not embed a chart in a tooltip.

options.text: In Dashboard > Actions, add a Go to Sheet action that runs on Hover.
options.rationale: Go to Sheet opens another sheet instead of embedding it in a tooltip.

options.text: In the Tooltip editor, choose Insert > Sheets and pick the sheet.
options.rationale: This creates a Viz in Tooltip: a whole sheet is shown inside the tooltip.

options.text: Turn on Include command buttons in the Tooltip dialog.
options.rationale: Command buttons add filter and View Data links; they do not embed a sheet.

explanation: A Viz in Tooltip puts a sheet inside the tooltip, inserted with Insert > Sheets in the Tooltip editor.

stem: A dashboard has a large panel of filter cards that clutters the screen. The analyst wants viewers to fold it away with a button. What should they use?

options.text: Use as Filter on the sheet that holds the panel
options.rationale: Use as Filter converts marks into filters and does not hide objects.

options.text: A data highlighter placed on the panel
options.rationale: A highlighter searches marks and does not fold away objects.

options.text: Add Show/Hide Button from the object's pop-up menu
options.rationale: The pop-up menu in the object's corner offers Add Show/Hide Button to show or hide it.

options.text: Apply to Worksheets > Only This Worksheet on each filter
options.rationale: This changes which sheets a filter affects; it does not hide the panel.

explanation: Show/Hide buttons let viewers collapse and expand an object such as a container of filters. They are added from the pop-up menu in the object's upper corner.

stem: A tooltip should offer viewers links to filter the view and to open View Data without leaving the dashboard. Which tooltip option provides them?

options.rationale: Command buttons add filtering options and View Data to the tooltip.
This selects all marks with the same value; it does not add buttons.
This embeds a sheet in the tooltip rather than adding command buttons.
This belongs to dashboard objects, not to tooltip settings.

explanation: Include command buttons shows filtering and View Data options in the tooltip. Allow selection by category is a separate option that selects marks sharing a value.

stem: Which two statements about tooltip settings are true? (Choose 2 answers.)

options.text: Include command buttons adds filtering and View Data options to the tooltip.
options.rationale: This is what the option provides.

options.text: Include command buttons makes the tooltip open a Go to URL action.
options.rationale: URL actions are defined under Dashboard > Actions.

options.text: Allow selection by category applies a filter to every sheet on the dashboard.
options.rationale: It selects marks; the scope of filtering is set by actions or filter cards.

options.text: Allow selection by category selects all marks with the same value.
options.rationale: This is what the option provides.

options.text: A tooltip can only contain text, never a chart.
options.rationale: A Viz in Tooltip places a whole sheet in the tooltip.

explanation: Both options live in the Tooltip editor: command buttons for filter and View Data options, and category selection for choosing all marks with the same value. Tooltips can also hold a sheet.

stem: Which two are controls a viewer can use directly on a dashboard to explore the data? (Choose 2 answers.)

options.rationale: Viewers search or pick values to make matching marks stand out.
Size is a layout choice for the author, not a control for exploring data.
Show Filter adds a card the viewer uses to restrict the data.
Device Preview is an authoring tool for layouts.
The navigator style belongs to stories, not dashboards.

explanation: Filter cards and highlighters give viewers interactive control. Fixed size, Device Preview and navigator style are authoring and story settings.

stem: Which three are options in the Apply to Worksheets submenu of a filter card? (Choose 3 answers.)

options.rationale: This opens the list of sheets, with an All on dashboard button.
Add to Context is on the filter's own menu and changes when it runs, not which sheets it applies to.
The filter applies to every sheet that uses the same data source.
Use as Filter is in the upper corner of a sheet on the dashboard, not in the filter card's menu.
This keeps the filter local to the current sheet.
Show/Hide buttons come from an object's pop-up menu and fold the object away.

explanation: The submenu offers Selected Worksheets, All Using Related Data Sources, All Using This Data Source and Only This Worksheet.

stem: On a dashboard, clicking a country on the map should dim the other values in the line chart instead of removing them. Which action type fits?

options.rationale: A highlight action keeps all marks and dims those that do not match.
A filter action removes marks that do not match from the target sheets.
Go to Sheet opens another sheet; it neither filters nor highlights.
This changes the members of a set and does not dim marks on its own.

explanation: Filter actions remove non-matching marks, while highlight actions keep every mark and dim the rest. When other values must stay visible, use highlight.

stem: From which menu does the analyst add a filter action to a dashboard?

options.text: The Tooltip dialog on the Marks card
options.rationale: The Tooltip dialog edits hover text and has no action list.
This is where actions of every type are created and edited.
The Layout pane sets item position and size.
The Analytics pane holds items like reference lines.

explanation: Dashboard > Actions lists a dashboard's actions; Add Action lets the analyst choose a type such as Filter or Highlight.

stem: Which Run action on setting fires an action as soon as the viewer moves the pointer over a mark, without clicking?

options.rationale: Select needs the viewer to click a mark.
Hover triggers the action when the pointer is over a mark.
Menu puts a link in the tooltip that the viewer must click.
This controls what happens when a filter selection is cleared; it is not a trigger.

explanation: Run action on offers Hover, Select and Menu. Hover reacts to the pointer, Select to a click and Menu to a link in the tooltip.

stem: A filter action runs from the map. When the viewer clears the selection, the other sheets should show all members again. Which setting is needed?

options.rationale: The sheets would stay filtered to the last selection.
The target sheets would show no marks.
This restores every member in the target sheets when the selection is cleared.
This setting belongs to parameter actions and does not apply to a filter action.

explanation: A filter action offers Leave the filter, Show all values or Exclude all values when the selection is cleared. Keep current value is for parameter actions.

stem: Which two are choices for what a filter action does when the selection is cleared? (Choose 2 answers.)

options.rationale: This option is offered by parameter actions.
The target sheets keep the previous filter.
This option is offered by parameter actions.
That decides how the action starts, not what happens on clearing.
The target sheets show no marks.

explanation: For filter actions the clear-selection choices are Leave the filter, Show all values and Exclude all values. Parameter actions have their own pair of options.
